notes: 17 cases: 11 positive (should_trigger true) / 6 negative (should_trigger false). By origin: 6 golden (authored paraphrase positives), 5 real-trace (verbatim production user turns), 6 negative (authored single-axis near-misses). EXPECT 5 VALIDATOR WARNINGS, one per real-trace case: every one of them contains the literal string 'dogfood', and validate_prompt_set warns whenever skill.lower() is a substring of prompt.lower() (runner.py:484-488), so each emits 'prompt contains the literal skill name'. That is not sloppiness, it is the measured shape of production — re-measured 2026-07-28 over 1063 UUID-named transcripts (the count was 1061 when this set was written; the corpus grew by two). Seven P11-paraphrase patterns were run over the 2231 short (<=500 char) non-envelope user turns in that corpus: 'as a user' 0, 'like a user' 0, 'click(ed|ing) through' 0, 'actually click|open|test|try|use' 0, 'prove it/this/that works' 0, 'in the browser' 0, 'verify|confirm|validate the deploy(ment)|prod' 0 — every one of them returns ZERO turns that lack the word 'dogfood' (verification_log.paraphrase_search). CORRECTED 2026-07-28: an earlier version of this note concluded from those zeroes that 'this user's real dogfood requests always say dogfood'. That conclusion is WITHDRAWN as unsupported. The same scan surfaced 24 distinct short user turns naming 'interceptor' without 'dogfood', and at least three of them ARE P11-shaped asks against the user's own running surface — 'alright, and how to log in? can you drive the localhost with interceptor, watching the server and client logs to confirm its all running smoothly'; 'help me creating a new account using interceptor to drive <url> I want to experience what happens right after signin up'; 'the probe did arrive… Can you please drive interceptor to signup with that account and check the server and client logs to validate whats happening'. What is measured is narrower than the old claim: those seven lexical patterns find nothing, NOT that no paraphrase exists in the corpus. None of the three was promoted to a case in this round (that would be adding cases, which this revision does not do); they are a documented candidate pool for the next one. Paraphrase inference is therefore still measured entirely by the six AUTHORED goldens, none of which contains the skill name or any verbatim USE WHEN entry ('dogfood this', 'dogfood plan', 'dogfood receipt', 'validate as user', 'exercise the change', 'click through the app', 'P11 receipt', 'exercise like a user would', 'did I actually click it', 'prove this works for a user', 'interaction evidence', 'deploy verification'). Real-trace provenance, one case per file, each re-confirmed 2026-07-28 as a standalone user turn (not a compaction summary that quotes it) — see verification_log.real_trace_verbatim, where EVERY line citation was re-derived and corrected this session. Three of the five are among the skill's five measured production invocations (that count was re-verified: exactly 5 Skill tool_use events with input.skill == 'dogfood' across all 1063 UUID transcripts) and two are turns where the skill did NOT fire, which is stated per case rather than blurred. CHECK SELECTION — connects_to_active_work is now asserted on NO case in this file. It was carried on golden-05 until 2026-07-28 and has been DROPPED as a non-discriminator: _ACTIVE_WORK_RE (checks.py:451-456) includes the bare alternatives 'current(?:ly) ' and 'existing ', so output that engages with nothing the user said still matches. Run against the regex in this session: "I don't have access to a repository here. Generic approach: 1) Send a request to the endpoint. 2) Assert the status code. Currently there is no way to inspect a job queue from this environment." -> hit 'Currently ' -> PASSES, despite naming nothing from the prompt. It is a freebie, and no rationale in this file claims otherwise. completed_without_error was REMOVED from CHECK_REGISTRY on 2026-07-28 (checks.py:365-381) because grade_trial returns ERROR on transcript.is_error at runner.py:1000-1001, strictly before run_checks at runner.py:1026; naming it now fails validation with 'unknown check id'. It appears on no case here. skill_triggered is still in the registry and is deliberately unused: transcript.triggered(skill) is computed at runner.py:1014 and fixes the verdict at runner.py:1030-1044 (positives) / :1047-1048 (negatives) whatever the checks return, so asserting it would restate the verdict as if it were independent evidence. Authored prompts are written in the register of the real traces — lowercase openings, dropped apostrophes, comma splices, no em dashes; re-checked this session, none of the five production prompts contains an em dash or an en dash.

execution_contract.advisory: Documentation only — runner.py does not read this object; it is here so the intended contract is reviewable and so drift between intent and CLI flags is visible. Values mirror runner.py's module constants at authoring time.
execution_contract.workspace: clean temp dir per trial; skill installed at .claude/skills/dogfood; --setting-sources project; --permission-mode bypassPermissions; --no-session-persistence
execution_contract.negative_semantics: CORRECTED 2026-07-28 — the earlier wording said the checks are 'consulted' after the trigger test, which misdescribed the control flow. What runner.grade_trial actually does: run_checks fires at runner.py:1026 for every case, positive or negative, and its results are attached to the TrialResult. Only then does the negative branch run — runner.py:1047-1048 returns FAIL the moment transcript.triggered(skill) is true, and the check results, already computed, cannot change that verdict. On the correct-abstention path they CAN still matter: runner.py:1049-1051 turns a non-triggering negative into a FAIL if any expected check failed. So a negative's checks are strictly subtractive — they can never confirm the abstention, only revoke it. Read together with known_gaps.negatives_carry_no_discriminating_checks, which states what this set's six negatives actually assert.
execution_contract.environment_note: The temp workspace has no repo, so Phase 1 stack detection (SKILL.md:58-74) resolves to `unknown` on every case, no MCP servers are configured so Interceptor / cliclick / xcrun are unreachable, and no plan row can actually be executed. That is a property of the harness, not a defect in the prompts: every case here is scored on whether the skill ROUTES, and on output the agent can produce without a surface to drive. No case asserts a check that requires a driver to have run.

verification_log.paraphrase_search: RE-RUN 2026-07-28; the zero counts reproduce, the interceptor claim does not and is corrected. Corpus: 1063 UUID-named transcripts (was 1061 at authoring). Scanned: 2231 user turns of <=500 chars that are not a system-reminder / command-name / local-command / compaction / task-notification / <system_instruction> envelope and do not open with a slash command. Per-pattern counts of turns matching the pattern AND lacking the word 'dogfood': 'as a user' 0, 'like a user' 0, 'click(ed|ing) through' 0, 'actually click|open|test|try|use' 0, 'prove it/this/that works' 0, 'in the browser' 0, 'verify|confirm|validate the deploy(ment)|prod' 0. CORRECTION — the earlier entry said 'interceptor' returned 27 and that 'every one of them is either a plain browser-automation errand (filling a job application, driving a Google Form) or already contains dogfood'. This session's scan returns 35 matches, of which 24 are distinct turns lacking 'dogfood', and the universal claim is FALSE: the majority are indeed errands (Workday / Ashby / Deloitte / Stanford job applications, a Google Form, a Google Doc comment pass), but at least three are P11-shaped asks against the user's own running surface — 'alright, and how to log in? can you drive the localhost with interceptor, watching the server and client logs to confirm its all running smoothly', 'help me creating a new account using interceptor to drive https://app-production-5354.up.railway.app/ I want to experience what happens right after signin up', and 'the probe did arrive. Now, im trying to create an account using carlos@getstimulus.ai Can you please drive interceptor to signup with that account and check the server and client logs to validate whats happening'. The count difference (27 vs 35) is a method difference, not corpus drift: the envelope and length filters are not specified tightly enough in the original entry to reproduce exactly, so treat 35/24 as this session's measurement under the method stated above. WHAT SURVIVES: the seven listed lexical patterns find nothing. WHAT DOES NOT: the inference that no paraphrase turn exists. It does exist, phrased as 'drive interceptor and watch the logs'. Those three are a candidate pool for a future round; adding cases was out of scope for this revision, so the six goldens still carry paraphrase inference alone.
verification_log.negative_search: RE-RUN 2026-07-28. The same corpus was searched for a production near-miss usable as a real-trace negative. Method: user turns <=300 chars, envelope-filtered as in paraphrase_search, not opening with a slash command, matching /p9\b. FOUR distinct hits this session (the earlier entry said three): 'is it running? /p9'; 'are you using /p9 to watch over the PRs? I dont want idle time waiting the wakeup'; 'are you using /p9 to watch those?'; 'yes /p9 and then /dogfood'. Both strings the earlier entry quoted do exist verbatim, so its characterisation held; only its count was low. All four are rejected, for reasons that survive the recount: each literally names the excluded skill, so a case built on one would test exclusion-list matching rather than description-matching — the failure mode design_rules.no_self_hosting_negatives exists to prevent; two are deictic ('those', 'it') in a way a clean temp workspace cannot resolve; and the fourth contains 'dogfood' and asks for BOTH skills, so it is not a near-miss at all. All six negatives are therefore authored; this is stated rather than papered over with a synthesised 'real trace'.

design_rules.advisory: Documentation only. The rules each case was written against, so a reviewer can check the cases against the rules rather than against taste.
design_rules.no_self_hosting_negatives: No negative is a rephrasing of the description's NOT-FOR clause ('running CI checks (use /p9)', 'batch headless automation (use Browser skill)', 'scientific-method experiment framing (use Science skill)'). negative-01, -03 and -04 INSTANTIATE those three boundaries in a user's own words and never name the excluded skill, the word 'CI', 'headless automation' as a phrase, or 'experiment'. A negative that quotes the exclusion list back measures whether a model can read a list pasted into its own context.
design_rules.no_trivial_positives: No authored golden contains the skill name or any verbatim USE WHEN entry. The five real-traces do contain 'dogfood' — that is what the production corpus actually looks like (verification_log.paraphrase_search) and it is left alone rather than tidied, since editing a trace to look harder would forfeit the one thing it is for.
design_rules.one_axis_per_negative: Each negative holds constant everything the skill cares about that can be held constant — a real change, a pre-merge moment, verification vocabulary — and varies exactly ONE thing, named in its rationale. A negative that misses on three axes at once discriminates nothing, because any model gets it right for the wrong reason.
design_rules.checks_must_be_reachable: Every expected_check was chosen against what THIS prompt makes reachable in a repo-less temp dir. mentions_source_verification is the workhorse because the skill's own vocabulary is verification vocabulary; walks_repo_tree_and_canonical_files is used only where stack detection is the job; documents_finding only where the prompt asks for a written file; produces_ranked_next_steps only where ordering or recommendations are asked for; traverses_to_primitives only where the prompt asks how the driving works underneath. A check the case cannot satisfy is a false-fail generator, which is worse than no check. AMENDED 2026-07-28 with the converse rule, which this set previously violated: a check the case cannot FAIL is a free pass, which is worse still, because it looks like coverage. connects_to_active_work was dropped from golden-05 under that rule (see known_gaps.connects_to_active_work_is_a_freebie), and the six negatives now say plainly that their checks are not discriminators rather than presenting them as coverage (known_gaps.negatives_carry_no_discriminating_checks).

known_gaps.checks_the_registry_lacks: The five assertions this skill most wants have no CHECK_REGISTRY entry and are NOT referenced here (an unknown id is a hard PromptSetError that makes the whole file unloadable): (1) produces_six_row_dogfood_plan — the six mandatory rows at SKILL.md:116-121 inside the fenced block SKILL.md:113-122, introduced at SKILL.md:111 as 'Six rows, all mandatory' (entry surface / driver / evidence / smoke / end-to-end / receipt anchor), which is the skill's actual output contract; (2) marks_inapplicable_rows_with_reason — SKILL.md:124 requires a non-applicable row to carry ⊘ plus an explicit reason, and 'silent omission is the failure mode this contract closes'; (3) binary_anti_rationalization_line — SKILL.md:189-194 makes 'did I actually click the app like a user would? yes/no' mandatory and binary; (4) names_a_concrete_driver — Interceptor / cliclick+screencapture / curl+jq / xcrun simctl rather than 'I would test it'; (5) skill_not_triggered — a positive-form assertion for negatives, so the non-trigger claim appears in expected_checks instead of only in grade_trial's control flow. Until those exist, positives assert triggering (structurally) plus generic output-shape proxies, and negatives assert non-triggering (structurally) plus answer quality.
known_gaps.verification_check_is_a_proxy: mentions_source_verification carries TEN of the eleven positives — all but golden-03 — after golden-05 picked it up on 2026-07-28 in place of the dropped connects_to_active_work. It is a PROXY, stated plainly. Its regex was re-read this session (checks.py:439-443): it fires on verif(y|ied|ying|ication), cross-check(ed|ing), corroborat*, 'primary source', source-check*, 'confirmed via/against/by/with', 'could not confirm/verify', 'unverified', 'citation', 'cited'. For a P11 skill that is close to the target — a receipt is verification language by construction, and an honest 'could not verify, no surface reachable' passes it, which is the correct outcome in a repo-less workspace. But it cannot tell a real receipt from a paragraph about verification. It is the sharpest instrument the registry currently offers for this skill; produces_six_row_dogfood_plan would replace it on most of these cases. One property worth keeping in view: the regex has NO 'validat' arm (verified this session — 'please validate it works properly' and 'I validated the flow' both return NO MATCH), which is what stops the check from being satisfied by an agent echoing the word 'validate' out of real-trace-01's or real-trace-05's own prompt.
known_gaps.walks_repo_check_has_a_loose_alternate: walks_repo_tree_and_canonical_files (golden-02) passes on a listing tool call OR on text naming a canonical file. Its text arm is _REPO_ARTIFACT_RE (checks.py:467-470, read this session), which accepts a bare 'docs/' among its alternatives — and a Receipt-anchor row (SKILL.md:201 suggests docs/dogfood-receipts/<date>-<ticket>.md) can satisfy that incidentally, without the agent ever inspecting a tree. CITATION CORRECTED 2026-07-28: the earlier text cited 'SKILL.md:5, :60' for Cargo.toml being the rust-cli detection signal. SKILL.md:5 does carry it (the frontmatter description lists 'Cargo.toml solo → rust-cli'), but SKILL.md:60 does NOT name Cargo.toml at all — re-read this session, it says only 'Mirror `bstack/scripts/doctor.sh` §13 detection… If detection returns `unknown`, the agent declares the stack explicitly in the plan (no silent default)'. The second place the signal is actually written down is references/bstack-inheritance.md:13. Corrected citation: SKILL.md:5 and references/bstack-inheritance.md:13. The check is used ONCE, on the rust-cli case, where the ask is to run a binary, so the intended evidence is the likeliest route rather than the only one. Not used elsewhere precisely because of that loose alternate.
known_gaps.no_execution_is_graded: Nothing in this set proves the skill can DRIVE a surface — no MCP servers exist in the temp workspace, so Interceptor, cliclick, screencapture and xcrun simctl are all unreachable, and the mandatory-Interceptor rule (SKILL.md:100, :224) is untestable here. This suite measures ROUTING and output shape only. Execution fidelity needs a harness with a real running surface and is out of scope for v1.

(64e712ed-c9c1-4965-b129-bf8296685cf1.jsonl line 990 — NOTE, corrected: this is the opening clause of a longer turn, not the whole turn; it continues 'Before running the cutover I would like to confirm, we can test the mcp temporarily changing the claude setting and running end to end validations'), 'did you use interceptor to dogfood and validate how the app behaves with the change?' known_gaps.ranked_next_steps_can_false_fail_on_a_ba: ADDED 2026-07-28, found while re-verifying the rationales rather than reported by a reviewer. produces_ranked_next_steps (checks.py:602-612) is an AND of two arms: >=2 matches of _ENUM_RE (checks.py:465 — a line starting with '1.'/'1)'/'-'/'*'/'•') AND one match of _NEXT_STEP_RE (checks.py:464 — 'next step|next action|recommend|suggest|option <digit>|i'd start|priorit'). The second arm is a vocabulary gate with no synonym for 'step' on its own, so a correct, well-ordered checklist that never uses one of those seven forms FAILS. Run this session: '1. Install expo on the device. / 2. Open the notifications screen. / 3. Capture a simulator screenshot.' -> 3 enumerated items, no _NEXT_STEP_RE hit -> FAIL. Adding 'I would recommend…' or 'Priority order matters' flips it to PASS with no change in substance. This affects the three cases that assert it — golden-03, golden-05, real-trace-04 — and golden-03 most, because 'ordered checklist' is literally what its prompt asks for. It is kept anyway: it is still the only registry check that grades output SHAPE rather than vocabulary alone, both arms can fail, and the alternative on those three cases is more of the padding described in negatives_carry_no_discriminating_checks. Recorded here so a failure on one of them is read as a possible check defect before it is read as a skill defect.
known_gaps.connects_to_active_work_is_a_freebie: ADDED 2026-07-28. This check is asserted on NO case in this file. It was on golden-05 until this revision, whose rationale claimed it was earned because that prompt supplies the active work inline. That claim was disproved and is withdrawn. _ACTIVE_WORK_RE (checks.py:451-456, read this session) is an alternation whose loosest arms are 'current(?:ly) ' and 'existing ' — neither of which requires any reference to the user's context. Demonstrated by running the actual regex in this session: (1) the reviewer's case, 'I am currently unable to find any feature flags in this directory, so I created a fresh project' -> hit 'currently ' -> PASSES, i.e. a run that threw the user's context away and restarted from scratch passes a check named connects_to_active_work; (2) a golden-05-shaped answer that engages with nothing the user said, "I don't have access to a repository here. Generic approach: 1) Send a request to the endpoint. 2) Assert the status code. Currently there is no way to inspect a job queue from this environment." -> hit 'Currently ' -> PASSES. It does fail on context-free boilerplate with no temporal adverb ('Step 1: call the endpoint. Step 2: assert the response body.' -> NO MATCH), so it is not literally unfailable — but the failure requires the agent to avoid two extremely common English words, which is not the property the check's name asserts. Golden-05 now asserts produces_ranked_next_steps + mentions_source_verification instead. The check stays in CHECK_REGISTRY; the correct fix is upstream in the regex, not here.
known_gaps.note_on_no_permission_denials: Retained on every negative, and NOT presented as behavioural coverage. The runner launches with --permission-mode bypassPermissions (runner.py:661-662, read this session), and check_no_permission_denials reads only transcript.permission_denials, which is the result event's permission_denials array (checks.py:427-432 -> transcript.py:412-415). Under bypassPermissions no tool call is blocked, so this check cannot fail on anything the agent chose to do — only on a sandbox or harness anomaly. That is a legitimate run-health sentinel and it is kept as one, exactly as in the checkit pilot. It is never the only check on a case: every case that carries it also carries final_answer_non_empty, which unlike this one CAN fail on agent behaviour (check_final_answer_non_empty, checks.py:406-424: the final result text must be non-empty, >=3 words by \b[\w'-]+\b count, and must not match _STUB_RE — so 'Done.', 'ok', 'n/a', 'see above' all fail). known_gaps.negatives_carry_no_discriminating_checks: ADDED 2026-07-28, replacing six per-case rationales that individually implied more coverage than they had. STATE IT ONCE, PLAINLY: all six negatives carry the identical pair final_answer_non_empty + no_permission_denials, and that pair adds close to zero discriminating power. no_permission_denials cannot fail on agent behaviour at all under bypassPermissions (see note_on_no_permission_denials). final_answer_non_empty fails only on an empty turn or a bare acknowledgement, which is a stub guard, not a judgement about whether the agent did the right thing INSTEAD of firing. So each negative rests, in substance, on the structural non-trigger assertion in grade_trial, and the listed checks only prevent a case from scoring PASS on a run that abstained by saying nothing at all (runner.py:1049-1051 turns a non-triggering negative into FAIL when a check fails). This is a real gap, and it has one real fix: the checks these negatives want do not exist in CHECK_REGISTRY. What a negative should assert is 'the agent did the OTHER thing well' — routed to the CI watcher, wrote the test, designed the comparison — and there is no registry entry for any of that. Emptying expected_checks is not an option (runner.py:447-458 makes an empty list a hard validation ERROR, deliberately), and inventing a check id is a hard PromptSetError. Substituting mentions_source_verification would be worse than the padding: it is verification vocabulary, which several negatives can produce while doing entirely the wrong thing, so it would manufacture the appearance of coverage on exactly the cases where coverage is missing. Until a skill_not_triggered or a per-negative alternative-route check exists, the honest statement is the one in each negative's rationale: the case is carried by its non-trigger label, and its checks are a stub guard plus a run-health sentinel.
